label: PF Backlog 491
title: Defect/RCCA: concurrent sessions allocate the SAME backlog id (local counters, no coordination) -> push rejected + merge conflict
body:
Source: hit during BI-PF-0456 delivery (2026-10-08).

DEFECT: two sessions allocated the SAME backlog id. A concurrent session (another worktree) pushed BI-PF-0455 (a
DOGFOOD e2e checker defect) to origin/develop; THIS session had allocated BI-PF-0455 for a different item (the
ensure_feature_item dataclass bug). The push was rejected (non-fast-forward) and the merge produced an add/add
conflict on data/backlog/items/BI-PF-0455.json. Resolved by renumbering this session's item to BI-PF-0456.

RCCA (5-Why):
1. Two different items shared id BI-PF-0455. 2. Each session computed next-id = max(local counters)+1 = 0455.
3. The id counter is a LOCAL per-worktree file (data/backlog/counters.json) with no cross-session coordination.
4. IS-PF-0036 requires a separate worktree per session, but separate worktrees still share ONE id space via the
counters they each read from develop. 5. Guard: id allocation must be collision-safe across concurrent sessions.

Guard (proposed, decide): pick one+ - (a) re-read/refresh counters from origin/develop immediately before
allocation and re-key on divergence; (b) reserve id ranges per worker/session (worker-prefixed suffix); or
(c) a merge/precheck audit that FAILS on duplicate ids across the integration branch. Long-term: allocate ids
from the shared remote (one authority), not a local counter.

Impact: cosmetic-ish (renumber works) but breaks automated delivery (push rejected, merge conflict), so it must
not recur as concurrency grows (worker plane).
